title: [Lean] Validate compact column fragments and their byte representation
body:
## Checked context and coverage

Explicit author-checked kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000 = 0.001672660197076918, at upstream main 0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea. These generic components do not change that exponent.

Three checked modules validate every original compact natural-column byte, match the complete ordered columns to an actual named dictionary entry, and prove the compact decimal/bracket/comma alphabet has exact one-byte UTF-8 representation in order.

Finite coverage: arbitrary finite dimension including zero, arbitrary natural magnitudes and list lengths. The fixed alphabet proof uses five ordinary closed decide sites, without selected-data decisions.

Conditional-interface coverage: success gives parser/AST equations, exact compact bytes, bounded ordered columns and the recovered binary operator with both inverses. Completeness retains the actual compact JSON parser equation and restricted permutation/rank-one factorization. The dictionary input is an AST; no structural source-span, dictionary-file containment or authenticated digest/key is established by this chunk. Logical ASCII/UTF-8 representation does not verify runtime extern implementations.

Full-theorem coverage: no actual selected-file success, general JSON parser correctness, physical executor/allocation/direction, precision, recursive cost or full multiplication/runtime theorem.

## Evidence and reproduction

Three unchanged sources total 20,894 bytes. Sixteen standard-only axiom probes and six complete printed types passed local kernel and independent exact-source/terminal review with no diagnostics. Public manifest binds hashes and complete observed evidence.

REPRODUCTION.md pins prepared Lean 4.21.0 and Mathlib 308445d7985027f538e281e18df29ca16ede2ba3 and gives an isolated bounded serial 19-module closure. The publication recipe was inspected, not rerun; no extra local CI preflight or archive rebuild.

## Overlap and attribution

Sixteen public prerequisites are referenced without copying: PR #1831 at 542f914ca0e5df4026341d08c84385cb1a71cfdf; #1879 at 981afe759f7dd206188b1c1a62250c6425bcd76a; #1927 at a5838afac3a2d69d802c2440cbfa7d160ca0b218; #1950 at d5aa485468f31fbcac3758ee63284c07da426cde. The new scope adds compact whole-byte equality, executed ordered fragment-to-entry matching and ASCII lowering. Unused ByteRecoveredProviderEntry, selected L450 applications and separate slice witnesses are excluded.

Credit: Lean Nat/String/UTF-8/JSON and Mathlib authors; Jeremy Kothe T16/PR514 and PR484/507 lineage; Rohan Arun PR1094; predecessor parser/chart/recovery components. James Chang with OpenAI assistance, Apache-2.0. No broad novelty claim.

Next useful obligation: execute a slice witness against the same original artifact, keeping literal containment distinct from identifying the structural JSON field span and authenticating the file.
